instruction: Make the body text on this slide italic.

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.hotkey('ctrl', 's'); time.sleep(0.5);

metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent attempted to underline content and change font color to dark red 2 on a slide with title, body text, and a table. It selected body text, applied underline, opened Character dialog and custom color picker, entered #B22222 (wrong color for 'Dark Red 2'). Then tried to format title and table but spent many turns struggling with color dialogs and table selection.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can select text in Impress text boxes, apply underline (Ctrl+U), open Format > Character dialog, navigate Font Effects tab, use custom color picker. Struggled with correct color identification and consistent formatting across multiple elements.
metadata.failure_analysis: Model used wrong hex color (#B22222 instead of LibreOffice's standard 'Dark Red 2'). Also failed to consistently format all elements (title + body + table). The multi-element + multi-format requirement was too complex.
metadata.task_rationale: Simplified to single formatting operation (italic) on single element (body text). Uses Ctrl+I shortcut similar to Ctrl+U which model demonstrated it can use. Tests basic text formatting capability.
metadata.explanation: Task requires making body text italic. Getter checks if all text runs in PlaceHolder 2 have italic=True. Metric returns partial credit based on proportion of italic runs.

scoring_breakdown.italic: 1.0 - All body text runs are italic (partial credit for partial coverage)

llm_judge_reasons: Getter correctly targets 'PlaceHolder 2' on slide 0, which is the standard body text placeholder in LibreOffice Impress, matching the instruction to check body text.
Getter properly reads italic property from all non-empty text runs using python-pptx, which is the correct API for checking font formatting.
Metric provides both full credit (all_italic=True) and partial credit (italic_runs/total_runs), which is appropriate for this task.
Postconfig correctly saves the file (Ctrl+S) before the getter reads it, ensuring the file state reflects the agent's changes.
Complete coverage: the instruction has a single requirement (make body text italic) and the evaluator checks exactly that.
Minor issue: the metric ignores the 'expected' parameter entirely and hardcodes the all_italic check. Functionally correct but does not validate against the expected rules dict.
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Consider having the metric use the 'expected' parameter (e.g., expected.get('all_italic')) instead of hardcoding the check, for better maintainability and consistency with the framework pattern.
